name: An Auckland garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: Auckland (Q37100), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban section in the northern half of Auckland: a lawn and a border of flax and evergreen hedging, a pōhutukawa and a tōtara over the fence, nīkau palms along the frontage and a kōwhai, a cabbage tree and an old apple tree in the garden, with green and golden bell frogs calling from the pond in spring and possums working the fruit trees after dark.

facts.text: Auckland has an oceanic climate under the Köppen classification (Cfb); under the Trewartha classification, and according to NIWA, the city is humid subtropical with warm summers and mild winters.

source.title: Wikipedia: Auckland
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Auckland", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Auckland's elevation runs from sea level to 196 metres, which is its highest point and the figure Wikidata records as the city's elevation.

source.title: Wikipedia: Auckland
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Auckland", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The green and golden bell frog was introduced to New Zealand in the 1860s by the Auckland Acclimation Society, and is now common in the part of the North Island north of Rotorua.

source.title: Wikipedia: Green and golden bell frog
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Green and golden bell frog", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: In contrast to Australia, where the green and golden bell frog has disappeared from about 90% of its former range, the frogs are abundant in New Zealand and are classified there as feral and unprotected.

source.title: Wikipedia: Green and golden bell frog
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Green and golden bell frog", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The tūī is an endemic honeyeater that will tolerate quite small remnant patches, regrowth, exotic plantations and well-vegetated suburbs, and feeds on the nectar, fruit and insects a garden offers all year.

source.title: Wikipedia: Tūī
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Tūī", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Introduced possums and rats significantly reduce the fruit available to kererū, and they also prey on kererū eggs and nestlings.

source.title: Wikipedia: Kererū
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Kererū", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The dark-flecked garden sunskink is native to eastern Australia and was accidentally introduced to New Zealand, where it is more common in suburban gardens than in adjacent native bushland.

source.title: Wikipedia: Lampropholis delicata
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Lampropholis delicata", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Wikidata records a population of about 1.47 million for Auckland.
